info.name: telvox chat — Mobile API v1
info.description:
# telvox chat — Mobile API v1

The API behind the telvox chat mobile app: sign-in, picking a WhatsApp number, the shared inbox, tickets and live updates. Base path: `{{base_url}}/api/mobile/v1`. Every request and response is JSON (`Accept: application/json`).

This API is private to the mobile app. It is not the partner API and is not listed in the public docs.

## Quick start

1. Import this collection and the **telvox chat — Mobile API (local)** environment; set `base_url`, `email`, `password`.
2. Run **1. Authentication → Login**. The test script saves `token` (and `challenge_token` if a second factor is needed — then run **Verify second factor**).
3. Run **2. Account → Businesses**, then **Numbers of a business**. The scripts save `business_user_id` and `waba_user_id`. (A manager, sub-user or number account skips this: it works on its own number.)
4. Every request in **4. Inbox** now works with `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` and `X-Waba-User-Id: {{waba_user_id}}`.

## Authentication

- `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` on everything except Login, Verify second factor and Resend code (set at collection level).
- One token per device (`device_uuid`). Signing in again on the same device replaces its token.
- A phone is signed out after **30 days without a request**, and in any case **90 days after it signed in** — rotating the token does not extend that.
- It is also signed out when the account's password, email, role, business or number changes, when the account is deleted, when a 6th device signs in (the longest-idle one goes), or from **Sign out one of my devices**. Every one of those gets `device.revoked` on the device channel (see Realtime).
- Partner API keys do not work here, and a phone token does not work on the partner API.

## Picking the number (`X-Waba-User-Id`)

Business owners, admins and resellers work on one WhatsApp number at a time, as in the web header: pick a business (**Businesses**), then a number (**Numbers of a business**), and send its id in `X-Waba-User-Id` on every inbox request. The number is checked on each request; the account's browser selection is never used or changed.

A manager, sub-user or number account is tied to its own number: omit the header or send that number's id.

## Statuses the app branches on

Auth and account answers carry a machine-readable `status`:

| status | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `authenticated` | 200 | Signed in; `token` is in the response |
| `two_factor_required` | 202 | Continue with Verify second factor |
| `password_reset_required` | 409 | Account still on a shared starting password — set one on the website |
| `role_not_allowed` | 403 | This account type cannot use the app |
| `email_unverified` | 403 | Verify the email first |
| `invalid_credentials` | 422 | Wrong email or password (same answer for an unknown email) |
| `invalid_code` / `challenge_expired` | 422 | Second factor wrong / challenge used or older than 10 minutes |
| `throttled` | 429 | Too many attempts |
| `waba_required` | 400 | Send `X-Waba-User-Id` |
| `waba_forbidden` | 403 | That number is not yours (or does not exist) |
| `number_unavailable` / `account_inactive` | 403 | The account's number or business is gone — sign in again |

## Errors any inbox request can return

| HTTP | Body | When |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | `{"message": "Unauthenticated."}` / `{"status": "unauthenticated", …}` | No, expired or revoked token |
| 400 | `{"status": "waba_required", …}` | Number header missing |
| 403 | `{"status": "waba_forbidden", …}` | Number not yours |
| 403 | `{"success": false, "reason": "plan_missing" \| "plan_expired" \| "billing_blocked", "message": …}` | Plan or billing |
| 403 | `{"message": "This feature is disabled in WhatsApp Ticketing mode."}` | Team-inbox endpoint while the number is in ticketing-only mode |
| 403 | `{"message": "User does not have the right permissions."}` | The route's permission is missing (named on each request) |
| 403 | `{"message": "Your plan does not include the Inbox."}` | Plan lacks the Inbox module (when the Inbox plan gate is on) |
| 429 | `{"message": "Too Many Attempts."}` | Rate limit |

Each request in this collection carries every one of these that applies to it as a saved example.

## Rate limits

- Sign-in, second factor and resend: 20 per minute per IP, plus 5 wrong passwords per email+IP and 5 wrong codes per account.
- Signed-in calls: 240 per minute per device.

## Realtime

Settings come from **Inbox config → realtime** (`key`, `host`, `port`, `scheme`, `auth_endpoint`, `device_channel`). Use Laravel Echo / the Pusher protocol against Reverb, authorising private channels at `auth_endpoint` with the bearer token and `X-Waba-User-Id`.

- Subscribe to the number's channels and to your **device channel**. On `device.revoked` disconnect and return to Login.
- Authorisation happens once, at subscribe: re-authorise after switching number.
- Send **Presence heartbeat** every `heartbeat_interval_seconds` while in the foreground.

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description: Sign-in runs the web login's checks in the same order: password, brand host, retired starting password, role, email verification, then the second factor. Every answer carries a `status` the app branches on.

request.description:
Signs a phone in. On `authenticated` the response carries the bearer token (the Postman test saves it as `{{token}}`). On `two_factor_required` continue with **Verify second factor** using `challenge_token`.

An unknown email and a wrong password get the identical `invalid_credentials` answer. Five wrong passwords per email+IP lock sign-in for a minute (shared with the web login).

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `email` | string | yes | email, max:255 | Account email. |
| `password` | string | yes | max:255 | Account password. |
| `device_uuid` | uuid | yes | uuid | The app's install id. Same value on every sign-in from this install, so signing in again replaces this device's token. |
| `platform` | integer | yes | in: 1 (ios), 2 (android) | config('mobile.device.platform'). |
| `device_name` | string | no | max:255 | Shown in the user's device list. |
| `app_version` | string | no | max:32 |  |
| `os_version` | string | no | max:32 |  |

response.name: 200 Authenticated
202 Second factor required
409 Shared starting password — set a new one on the website
403 Role cannot use the app
403 Email not verified
422 Wrong email or password
422 Validation failed
429 Too many sign-in attempts

request.description:
Answers the challenge from **Login**. Send the authenticator / WhatsApp / email code, or a recovery code with `recovery: true`. A challenge works once and lives 10 minutes; five wrong codes per account lock it until the challenge expires.

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `challenge_token` | string | yes | size:64 | From the 202 Login response. |
| `code` | string | yes | max:64 | 6-digit code, or a recovery code. |
| `method` | string | no | in: totp, whatsapp, email | Defaults to the account's default method. |
| `recovery` | boolean | no | boolean | true when `code` is a recovery code. |

response.name: 200 Authenticated

422 Wrong code
422 Challenge expired or already used

request.description:
Start-up settings for the picked number — the same payload the React inbox receives (number details, Direct Send, masking, AI-assist flags, notification rules) — plus the public websocket settings and the heartbeat interval. Never contains the realtime secret.

`capabilities` says what this account may do, so the app can hide the rest instead of meeting a 403: `actions` lists every inbox endpoint (`name`, `method`, `path`, `allowed`) judged by the same checks the endpoint applies — its permission, WhatsApp Ticketing-only mode and the Inbox plan module; `permissions` holds the checks made inside handlers (assign, unassign, see all conversations, multiple assignment, tracked links, edit contact fields); `message_types` says which `message_type` values (plus `template` and `direct_send`) this number can send — product types also need a catalogue (*Catalogues*); `media_limits` are the extensions and byte sizes *Send a message* enforces. Advisory: computed at start-up, so re-read config after a plan or role change; the endpoints still refuse on their own.

item.name: 3. Realtime
item.description:
Live updates use Laravel Echo / Pusher protocol against Reverb with the settings from **Inbox config** (`realtime`).

Subscribe to:
- the number's private channels (e.g. `private-receive.message.{waba_user_id}.{wa_id}`, `private-inbox.user.list.update.{waba_user_id}.{phone}`, `private-notification.{waba_user_id}`)
- **ticket inbox list updates** on your own channel `private-ticket.agent.{your user id}` (the `id` from **Me**). Events: `.ticket.inbox.new`, `.ticket.user.list.update`, `.ticket.inbox.message.received`, `.ticket.inbox.message.sent`, `.ticket.inbox.message.status`. Each ticket's events are sent only to the users allowed to see that ticket (same rule as the ticket endpoints), so no client-side filtering by department or team is needed. You can only join your own agent channel.
- for an open ticket: `private-ticket.message.{ticket_id}` (its messages) and `private-ticket.{ticket_id}` (its notes) — authorised only for tickets you can reach.
- **your device channel** `private-mobile.device.{device_id}` (from `realtime.device_channel`). On event `device.revoked` the phone has been signed out: disconnect the socket and return to Login.

Channel authorisation is checked once, at subscribe: re-authorise channels after switching number.

item.name: 4. Inbox
item.description: The React inbox's own endpoints (routes/inbox.php), reached with the phone's token. Every request carries `X-Waba-User-Id: {{waba_user_id}}`.

item.name: AI: fill custom fields from the conversation

header.description: The WhatsApp number this request acts for. A manager, sub-user or number account may only send its own (or omit it).

request.description:
Reads the conversation and **writes** values into this contact's still-empty custom fields that are enabled for AI extraction on this number (manual mode). Nothing already filled is touched. **Permission:** `ai-extract-fields`, plus `update-contact-field-value` (checked in the controller → 403).

`data.filled` lists the fields written (`field_id`, `name`). When nothing was attempted, `data.skipped` explains why: `extraction_off` (not enabled for this number), `nothing_to_fill` (no enabled empty fields), `no_conversation`.

A contact not visible to the caller returns 404 `Message not found`.

**Common refusals:** 409 `Select a business and WhatsApp number before using AI Assist.` when no business resolves; 403 `AI Assist is switched off for this business. A business owner can enable it in Settings.` (business consent not granted); 403 `This AI feature has been switched off.` (feature disabled); 422 `{success:false, blocked:true}` when the provider's safety filter declines; 503 `The AI service is unavailable right now. Please try again.` for any other provider failure. FormRequest validation failures return Laravel's standard **422** `{message, errors}`.

**Permission:** `ai-extract-fields`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contact_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|min:1 | Contact id visible to the caller. |

request.description:
Drafts a reply from the recent conversation (last 20 messages / 6000 chars of context) for the agent to edit. It is **never sent** — post it to *Send a message* yourself. **Permission:** `ai-generate-reply`.

`instruction` (optional, ≤2000 chars) steers the draft. 422 when the conversation is empty; 404 when the contact is not visible.

**Common refusals:** 409 `Select a business and WhatsApp number before using AI Assist.` when no business resolves; 403 `AI Assist is switched off for this business. A business owner can enable it in Settings.` (business consent not granted); 403 `This AI feature has been switched off.` (feature disabled); 422 `{success:false, blocked:true}` when the provider's safety filter declines; 503 `The AI service is unavailable right now. Please try again.` for any other provider failure. FormRequest validation failures return Laravel's standard **422** `{message, errors}`.

**Permission:** `ai-generate-reply`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contact_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|min:1 | Contact id visible to the caller. |
| `instruction` | string | no | nullable\|string\|max:2000 | Optional guidance for the draft. |

request.description:
Translates one message of a conversation the caller can see. `tenant_message_id` is the message's internal row id (the `id` in the messages list), not the wamid. Translations are stored: asking again for the same message + language returns the stored one (`cached: true`) unless `regenerate: true`. `unchanged: true` means the result equals the source (names, codes) — show "nothing to translate". **Permission:** `ai-translate-message`.

`target_language`: free-text language name, ≤40 chars, letters/marks/spaces/hyphens/parentheses only. 404 when the message doesn't exist or its conversation isn't visible; 422 when it has no text (e.g. image without caption).

**Common refusals:** 409 `Select a business and WhatsApp number before using AI Assist.` when no business resolves; 403 `AI Assist is switched off for this business. A business owner can enable it in Settings.` (business consent not granted); 403 `This AI feature has been switched off.` (feature disabled); 422 `{success:false, blocked:true}` when the provider's safety filter declines; 503 `The AI service is unavailable right now. Please try again.` for any other provider failure. FormRequest validation failures return Laravel's standard **422** `{message, errors}`.

**Permission:** `ai-translate-message`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tenant_message_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|min:1 | Internal message id. |
| `target_language` | string | yes | required\|string\|max:40\|regex:/^[\pL\pM\s\-()]+$/u | e.g. Hindi, Gujarati, Portuguese (Brazil). |
| `regenerate` | boolean | no | nullable\|boolean | Ignore the stored translation and overwrite it. |

request.description:
Changes who owns a conversation. Behaviour depends on whether **multiple-user chat assignment** is enabled for the contact's number (check `multiple_assignment_enabled` from *Get contact details*).

**Single-assignment mode** — body `user_id`:
- `user_id` must be present; an integer assigns, `null` unassigns.
- Assigning needs permission `inbox-contact-assign`; unassigning needs `inbox-contact-unassign` (checked in the controller → 403, not route middleware).
- Managers / sub-users may only assign to users in their own assignable tree (403 otherwise).

**Multiple-assignment mode** — body `user_ids` (array, may be empty):
- Needs permission `multiple-user-chat-assignment` (403 otherwise).
- The list replaces the current assignees; an empty array clears all (needs `inbox-contact-unassign`).

When the assignment is cleared the conversation goes to the bot (`conversation_owner_type` 1) if a published chatbot flow or the AI Messenger bridge can answer on that number, otherwise it is left unassigned (`conversation_owner_type` 0). Assigning sets it to human (2). A CHAT_LOG message is written into the thread (`newLog`), broadcast live, and the `contact_updated` (and, if a previous assignee was replaced, `agent_abandoned`) automation triggers fire.

`ai_bot_synced`: `null` when the number is not bridged to the AI Messenger bot; otherwise `true/false` for whether the takeover (assign to human) / release (unassign) call to the bot succeeded.

Contact lookup: business-scoped, and for managers / sub-users / number accounts also limited to their own number (404).

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `user_id` | integer|null | yes | single-assign mode only: present, nullable, integer, exists in users with the caller's business_user_id | User to assign to; null = unassign (hand to bot when one can answer). |
| `user_ids` | array<integer> | yes | multi-assign mode only: present, array; each integer and a user of the caller's business | Full replacement list of assignees; [] clears. |

request.description:
Blocks the contact on WhatsApp (Meta's own block list for the number) so they can no longer message the business.

**Permission:** route requires `create-block`.

Contact visibility: same business, same number, and for a manager/sub-user without `inbox-tab-all-contacts` the chat must be assigned to them (or unassigned) — otherwise 404.

422 cases pass through the refusal text: contact has no phone number; the number is not connected to the Cloud API; the number reached its blocked-user limit (`config('block.limits.max_blocked')`); or Meta refused (e.g. the user has not messaged in the last 24 hours — Meta's own wording is returned). No request body.

**Permission:** `create-block`

request.description:
Downloads the whole conversation as a CSV file (`Content-Disposition: attachment`), filename `{slug-of-profile-name}-{YYYY-MM-DD}.csv` (falls back to `chat-{id}`). Reactions are excluded.

Columns: `Date & time` (d/m/y H:i:s), `Direction` (Outgoing/Incoming), `Sender` (agent name or "System" for outbound; contact name, else masked number, for inbound), `Message type`, `Message`, `Status` (Pending/Sent/Delivered/Read/Failed/Error), `Failed reason`.

**Permission:** route requires `export-chat`.

Contact visibility gate as in Block; a miss is `abort(404)`, which on the mobile API renders Laravel's JSON error `{"message": ""}` (empty message; with APP_DEBUG on it includes exception details).

**Permission:** `export-chat`

request.description:
Creates or replaces one custom-field value on a contact. **Permission:** `update-contact-field-value`.

Send JSON for text/select/date types and `multipart/form-data` for file/image/video types. On success re-evaluates segments and fires the *custom field changed* automation trigger (with old and new value).

Field-level failures (too long, duplicate multi-select values, bad file type/size) come back as **400** with a single `message` and no `errors` object.

**Permission:** `update-contact-field-value`

request.description:
Creates a tag on the current number, or — when `id` is sent — updates that tag's name (and re-homes it to the current number). Does **not** attach it to a contact; use *Attach a tag to a contact*.

Note: the declared validation is never enforced. A missing `name` reaches the database and returns the 500 response; `id` is not checked against the caller's own tags.

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | declared required (not enforced) | Tag name. |
| `id` | integer | no | sometimes (not enforced) | Existing tag id to rename. |

request.description:
Returns one page of the inbox conversation list for the selected WhatsApp number, newest activity first (`last_message_date` desc). This is the left-hand chat list of the inbox.

**Response is a bare JSON array** (no `success`/`data` envelope).

Scoping:
- Always limited to the number in `X-Waba-User-Id`.
- Managers / sub-users without `inbox-tab-all-contacts` only see chats assigned to themselves or their sub-tree (except `listType=unassigned`, which shows every unassigned chat so it can be picked up).
- Every list except `closed` shows open conversations only (`conversation_status = 1`).

Per-row extras added by the server: `display_wa_id` (masked when number masking is on for this viewer — use `wa_id` for sending), `is_dnd`, `is_blocked`, `unread_message_count` capped at 99, `last_message` (last inbound/outbound message, change-log rows excluded), and `assigned_user_ids` **only when multiple-user chat assignment is enabled** for the number.

`favourite` is a JSON-encoded string array of user ids who starred the chat. Validation: none — unknown values are ignored, there is no 400 from this endpoint.

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `listType` | string | no | one of: all, mychats, unread, unassigned, favourite, closed (anything else behaves like all) | all = every open chat; mychats = assigned to me (or to the WABA number user); unread = unread_message_count != 0; unassigned = no assignee (and, in multi-assign mode, no row in the multi-assignment table); favourite = starred by me; closed = closed conversations (conversation_status = 0). |
| `search` | string | no | free text | LIKE match on profile_name or wa_id. |
| `tags` | array<integer> | no | array of tag ids; ignored if not an array | Only contacts carrying any of these tags. |
| `assignedTo` | integer | no | user id | Only contacts assigned to this user (multi-assign aware). |
| `limit` | integer | no | default 30 (no max enforced) | Page size. |
| `offset` | integer | no | default 0 | Rows to skip. |

request.description:
Everything the conversation header and right-hand panel need for one contact: the full contact row (with `tags`, `notes` newest first each with its `user`, `country_flag`, masked `display_wa_id`, `assigned_user_ids`), the current assignee, users the caller may assign to, and capability flags.

Key fields in `data`:
- `assignUser`: the single assignee (User object, or null).
- `child_user_ids`: ids in the caller's own tree — the client shows the composer only when the chat's assignee is in this list (or the caller can see all).
- `users`: assignable users (role is_user=4 / is_subuser=5 / is_manager=6; sub-users only see their own department); the caller is renamed "You"; `role_name` is "User" / "Manager" / "Sub user".
- `multiple_assignment_enabled`, `assignedUsers`, `assigned_user_ids`: multi-assign state (empty when disabled).
- `ai_bot_enabled` / `ai_bot_label`: whether "Assign to bot" may be offered and its label.
- `can_assign_contact` (`inbox-contact-assign`), `can_export_chat` (`export-chat`), `can_add_dnd` (`list-dnd`), `can_remove_dnd` (`delete-dnd`), `can_block` (`create-block`), `can_unblock` (`delete-block`).
- `is_dnd`, `is_blocked`, `is_favourite` (for the caller), `waba_user_phone`.

400 when `contact_id` is missing or not in the business; 404 when it exists but is not visible to the caller (other number, or a manager/sub-user's chat assigned to someone outside their tree).

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contact_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|exists:contacts_masters_{business},id | Contact id. |

request.description:
One-shot transition used when the agent moves from one chat to another: closes `previous_contact_id` (decrements its `is_open`), opens `contact_id` (increments `is_open`, records viewer) and marks it read (zeroes `unread_message_count`, clears ticket unread counters for that contact, and sends the WhatsApp read receipt for the latest unreplied inbound message).

Both fields are optional. Same id for both → no close (no double count). `contact_id` omitted → only the close happens. A contact that is not found (other business / other number for tied roles) is simply skipped — the response reports `null` for it instead of erroring.

`data`: `opened` = contact id opened or null, `closed` = contact id closed or null, `marked_read` = boolean.

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contact_id` | integer | no | nullable\|integer | Chat being entered. |
| `previous_contact_id` | integer | no | nullable\|integer | Chat being left. |

request.description:
Stored custom-field values of one contact (or one ticket), across all value tables (text, textarea, multi, single, date, file). `data` is an **object keyed by custom field id**; each value row embeds its `custom_field` definition. Shape of a value depends on the table: `value` (text/textarea/single/multi — multi is a comma-separated string), `start_date`/`end_date` (date types), or `url`/`name`/`size`/`type`/`mime` (file types; `url` is a path on the public disk, e.g. prefix with `{APP_URL}/storage/`). Empty result → `[]` (empty JSON array).

Pass `contact_id` or `ticket_id` (ticket wins). `contact_id` must exist in the business's contacts table.

With `ticket_id` the ticket must be one you can reach (**404** otherwise).

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contact_id` | integer | no | required\|integer\|exists:contacts_masters_{business},id when ticket_id is absent | Contact. |
| `ticket_id` | integer | no | integer (not validated further) | Ticket (ticket inbox). |

request.description:

| `ticket_id` | integer | no | any truthy value (not validated) | Ticket (ticket inbox). |

request.description:
Saves a date, datetime or date-range custom field (types 5, 6, 7) into `start_date` / `end_date`. Sending both as null clears the value.

Pass `contact_id` (team inbox) **or** `ticket_id` (ticket inbox). When `ticket_id` is present it wins: the value is keyed by ticket and `contact_id` is ignored; otherwise `contact_id` is required and must exist in the business's contacts table (`exists:contacts_masters_{business}`). `customFieldId` must belong to the caller's business; `ticket_id` must be a ticket of the caller's business. Writes upsert one row per (contact|ticket, field). For a contact write the app also re-evaluates dynamic segments and fires the `custom_field_changed` automation trigger.

**Permission:** route requires `update-contact-field-value`. Validation errors return 400 with `message` = first error. On a contact write, `data` includes the loaded `custom_field` definition (on a ticket write it does not). Note: the endpoint does not check that the field's type matches this endpoint — use the endpoint matching the field type (see *Get custom field definitions*).

**Permission:** `update-contact-field-value`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `customFieldId` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|exists:custom_fields,id (caller's business) | Custom field id. |
| `contact_id` | integer | no | required\|integer\|exists:contacts_masters_{business},id unless ticket_id given | Contact (team inbox). |
| `ticket_id` | integer | no | integer, ticket of caller's business; takes precedence over contact_id | Ticket (ticket inbox). |
| `start` | string (date) | no | nullable\|date | Date / datetime / range start (e.g. 2026-12-12 or 2026-12-12 18:30). |
| `end` | string (date) | no | nullable\|date | Range end (daterange fields only). |

request.description:
Saves up to 100 custom-field values for one contact or ticket in a single, **all-or-nothing** request (one DB transaction). The server decides the value table from each field's type — not from the client:
- text / textarea / single (types 1,2,3,8,9,12,13,14): use `value`.
- multi (types 4,10,11): use `values` (array); stored comma-joined. (`value` is ignored for these.)
- date (types 5,6,7): use `start` / `end`.
- file types (15,16,17) cannot be saved here → field error "This field cannot be saved here."; upload them with *Store file value*.

Field-level problems are reported in `fieldErrors` keyed by custom field id and nothing is written. On success `data` is an object keyed by field id with the saved row, and `saved` lists the field ids. For a contact the app re-evaluates segments once and fires a `custom_field_changed` automation per field.

Pass `contact_id` (team inbox) **or** `ticket_id` (ticket inbox). When `ticket_id` is present it wins: the value is keyed by ticket and `contact_id` is ignored; otherwise `contact_id` is required and must exist in the business's contacts table (`exists:contacts_masters_{business}`).

**Permission:** route requires `update-contact-field-value`.

**Permission:** `update-contact-field-value`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contact_id` | integer | no | required\|integer\|exists:contacts_masters_{business},id unless ticket_id given | Contact. |
| `ticket_id` | integer | no | integer, ticket of caller's business; takes precedence | Ticket. |
| `values` | array<object> | yes | required\|array\|min:1\|max:100 | One entry per field. |
| `values.*.customFieldId` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|exists in caller's business custom_fields | Field id. |
| `values.*.value` | string|null | no | nullable | For text/textarea/single fields. |
| `values.*.values` | array<string> | no | nullable\|array; duplicates rejected | For multi fields. |
| `values.*.start` | string (date) | no | nullable\|date | For date fields. |
| `values.*.end` | string (date) | no | nullable\|date | For daterange fields. |

request.description:
Uploads a file for an image / document / video custom field (types 15, 16, 17) — **multipart/form-data**. Replaces (and deletes) any previous file for that field. Stored on the public disk under `customField/{number phone}/`; `url` in the response is that relative path (public URL = `{APP_URL}/storage/{url}`).

Per-type checks (by file extension and size):
- image (15): jpeg, jpg, png; max 5 MB.
- document (16): txt, xls, csv, xlsx, doc, docx, ppt, pptx, pdf; max 100 MB.
- video (17): 3gp, mp4; max 16 MB.
(Other field types are not checked.) The server's PHP upload limits may reject large files earlier.

Pass `contact_id` (team inbox) **or** `ticket_id` (ticket inbox). When `ticket_id` is present it wins: the value is keyed by ticket and `contact_id` is ignored; otherwise `contact_id` is required and must exist in the business's contacts table (`exists:contacts_masters_{business}`). `customFieldId` must belong to the caller's business; `ticket_id` must be a ticket of the caller's business. Writes upsert one row per (contact|ticket, field). For a contact write the app also re-evaluates dynamic segments and fires the `custom_field_changed` automation trigger.

**Permission:** route requires `update-contact-field-value`. Response `data` has no embedded `custom_field`.

**Permission:** `update-contact-field-value`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | file | yes | required\|file; type/size per field type (see description) | Upload. |
| `customFieldId` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|exists in caller's business custom_fields | Field id. |
| `contact_id` | integer | no | required\|integer\|exists:contacts_masters_{business},id unless ticket_id | Contact. |
| `ticket_id` | integer | no | integer, ticket of caller's business | Ticket. |

request.description:
**Permission:** any one of `list-ticket-inbox`, `create-ticket-inbox`, `edit-ticket-inbox`, `delete-ticket-inbox` (route middleware).

Sets the ticket's disposition (outcome code). Requires manage-ticket rights (403 otherwise). Writes a change-log line 'Disposition set to "X" (category: Y)' and broadcasts it. Validation errors return **422** with `errors` only. No try/catch: unexpected errors fall through to the framework's 500 `{"message": "Server Error"}`.

**Which tickets you can reach.** Every endpoint that takes a ticket id uses one rule, the same one the list uses: the ticket must be on your business and the selected number; a manager or sub-user also sees only their own tickets, their team's tickets in their Allowed Ticketing Departments, unassigned tickets in those departments, and unassigned tickets in the number's default department. A ticket with no department counts as in every department. Business owner, number account and super-admin see every ticket of the number. A ticket outside that rule is a **404**.

**Permission:** `list-ticket-inbox|create-ticket-inbox|edit-ticket-inbox|delete-ticket-inbox`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `disposition_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|exists:tkt_dispositions,id where waba_user_id = active number | Disposition id from List dispositions. |

| `type` | string | yes | required\|in:media,document,link | media = images + videos; document; link. |
| `search` | string | no | nullable\|string | Filter by file name / URL. |

request.description:
Uploads a file to the server's public storage and returns its public URL. Use the result as a template header: pass `data.file_url` as `variables.mediaTemplate.header_media.file_url` (and `data.file_name` as `new_file_name`) to *Send a template to a contact*. This does **not** send anything.

**multipart/form-data**. Limits:
* any file: max 100 MB (`max:102400` KB)
* `type=image`: extension jpeg/jpg/png (case-sensitive check), max 5 MB
* `type=video`: extension 3gp/mp4, max 16 MB
* `type=document` (default when omitted): no extension check, max 100 MB

For sending a file directly in a chat, attach it to *Send a message* (`media`) instead.

| `file` | file | yes | required\|file\|max:102400 | The upload. |

request.description:
Messages of one conversation, paged **backwards from the newest**: `offset` 0 is the latest `limit` messages; the page is then returned in chronological order (oldest → newest, ties by id). Increase `offset` by `limit` to load older history; use *Count messages* to know when to stop. Reaction messages are excluded (reactions are inside each message's `reaction` JSON string).

Row fields: `type` 1 outbound / 2 inbound / 3 change-log (`message_type` "CHAT_LOG"); `message_status` 0 pending, 1 sent, 2 delivered, 3 read, 4 failed, 5 error; `message_source` (outbound) 0 inbox, 1 broadcast, 2 automation, 3 chatbot, 4 api, 5 commerce; `sender_name` = agent name; `contextual_*` = the quoted message when this is a reply; `sent_by_ai` 1 when an AI chatbot composed it. `message_body_json` is a JSON string (for templates its `preview` array is re-ordered HEADER, ORDER_STATUS, BODY, FOOTER, BUTTONS, CAROUSEL). Timestamps are raw DB strings.

Contact must be visible to the caller (number + assignment rules) else 404.

On a number in ticketing-only mode a manager or sub-user gets only the messages on tickets they can reach (plus messages on no ticket); the business owner, number account and super-admin get every message of the contact.

### Paging by message and catching up (recommended for the app)
Offsets shift when a message arrives mid-scroll. Page by message instead — each takes `limit` and must not be combined with `offset` or with each other (**400**):
* `before_id` — older history: the `limit` messages just before that message. Start from `meta.oldest_id` of the page you have.
* `after_id` — what arrived after a message, oldest first. Start from `meta.newest_id`.
* `updated_since` (ISO-8601) — every message created **or changed** (status, reaction, edit) at or after that time, ordered by change. Pass `meta.sync_from` from your previous response; it is inclusive, so merge rows by `id`. If `meta.has_more` is true, call again with the new `meta.sync_from` **and** `updated_after_id` = `meta.sync_after_id` — that carries the catch-up past a second holding more changes than one page (without it the same page comes back). Drop `updated_after_id` once `has_more` is false.

Cursors order by (`created_at`, `id`), so messages sharing a second never fall between pages. A cursor message not in this conversation (or not visible to you) → **404 `Message not found`**.

Every response carries `meta`: `has_more` (more rows in the paging direction), `oldest_id`, `newest_id`, `sync_from` (when this read began — store it for the next `updated_since`), `sync_after_id` (only mid catch-up: the last id returned, to send as `updated_after_id`; otherwise null).

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contact_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer | Contact. |
| `limit` | integer | no | integer\|min:1\|max:100; default 15 | Page size. |
| `offset` | integer | no | integer\|min:0; default 0 | Messages to skip from the newest. |
| `before_id` | integer | no | integer\|min:1; not with offset, after_id, updated_since | Older page: messages before this message id. |
| `after_id` | integer | no | integer\|min:1; not with offset, updated_since | Newer page: messages after this message id, oldest first. |
| `updated_since` | string | no | ISO-8601 date-time; not with offset; required with updated_after_id | Catch up: messages created or changed at or after this time (use `meta.sync_from`). |
| `updated_after_id` | integer | no | integer\|min:1; only with updated_since | Continue a catch-up after this message id within the `updated_since` second (use `meta.sync_after_id` while `has_more` is true). |

request.description:
Creates a contact on the WhatsApp number in `X-Waba-User-Id`. `wa_id` is stored as `country` + `phone` concatenated (send `country` as the dialling code without `+`, e.g. `91`).

* Business / admin / reseller callers: the contact is assigned to the number itself; managers/sub-users: assigned to themselves.
* Fires the *contact created* automation trigger and re-evaluates segments.
* **Validation failures return HTTP 200** with `success: false` (not 400/422) — check `success`.
* A duplicate `phone` on the same number is refused (`The phone number already exists.`).

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | required | Profile name shown in the inbox. |
| `phone` | string | yes | required; must not already exist on this number | National number without country code. |
| `country` | string | yes | required | Country dialling code without `+` (e.g. `91`). Prepended to `phone` to form `wa_id`. |

request.description:
Sends a WhatsApp emoji reaction to a message on behalf of the business number and stores it in the message's `reaction` list (one reaction per business number — a new emoji replaces the previous one). Broadcasts the update to other viewers. Sending an empty `emoji` asks WhatsApp to remove the reaction; use *Remove reaction* for that.

`message_id` is the WhatsApp message id (`wamid…`) of a message on the selected number; `phone` is the recipient's WhatsApp number (the contact's `wa_id`).

**Note:** when the provider rejects the reaction the endpoint answers **HTTP 200** with `success: false` ("Meta not allowed this message action.").

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `message_id` | string | yes | required\|string | WhatsApp message id (wamid). |
| `emoji` | string | no | nullable\|string\|max:10 | Emoji to react with. |
| `phone` | string | yes | required\|string | Contact's WhatsApp number (wa_id). |

request.description:
Removes a reaction: sends an empty reaction to WhatsApp, then deletes the entry from the message's `reaction` list and broadcasts the change. **DELETE with a JSON body.**

request.description:
Sends a free-form (session) message from the WhatsApp number to a contact. This is the inbox composer's send.

**Required in the body:** `waba_user_id` — must be the number in `X-Waba-User-Id` (or one the caller owns); anything else is refused with **403** and an empty message. `contact_id` and `wa_id` must name the **same** contact on that number in the caller's business, otherwise **404 `Contact not found`**.

**Content type:** JSON for every type except media. To send a file, use `multipart/form-data` with the file in `media` (the `message_type` still has to be present but is overridden by the file's sniffed MIME type).

### Message types (`message_type`)
| value | sends | needs |
|---|---|---|
| `text` (or any value not listed below) | text message | `body`; optional `contextual_reply_id` (wamid) to reply to a message |
| *(file in `media`)* image | image + caption | jpeg/jpg/png ≤ 5 MB; `body` = caption |
| *(file in `media`)* video | video + caption | 3gp/mp4 ≤ 16 MB; `body` = caption |
| *(file in `media`)* anything else | document + caption, original filename kept | pdf/doc/docx/xls/xlsx/ppt/pptx/txt ≤ 100 MB |
| `address` | address request (interactive `address_message`) | `address_country` (ISO-2, e.g. `IN`); `body`; optional `header`, `footer` |
| `location` | location **request** (asks the customer to share their location) | `body` |
| `send_location` | a location pin | `location` object `{latitude, longitude, name, address}` (object or JSON string) |
| `single_product` | one catalogue product | `singleProduct` (product id), `catalog_id`; `body`; optional `footer` |
| `multiple_product` | product list | `multipleProduct` (comma-separated product ids), `catalog_id`; `body`; optional `header`, `footer` |
| `catalogue` | catalogue message | `singleProduct` (thumbnail product id); `body`; optional `footer` |
| `call_permission_request` | asks permission to call the customer | `body` |

Not supported by this endpoint: audio/voice notes (an audio file fails the document extension check), stickers, contact cards, reply buttons/lists, and templates (use *Send a template to a contact*). `single_product`, `multiple_product`, `catalogue` and `call_permission_request` are only implemented for numbers on the Interakt provider; on an Aisensy number the server errors (500).

### Direct Send (beta)
Add `direct_send_category` (`utility` or `authentication`) to send a **text** message as a business-initiated message outside the 24-hour window, without a template. Optional `direct_send_ttl` (seconds; utility 30–43200, authentication 30–900) and `direct_send_template_name` (utility only, `^[a-z0-9_]+$`, ≤512). The number must be onboarded to Direct Send and on the Aisensy/Interakt provider. Body ≤1024 chars.

### Other optional fields
`ticket_id` (ticket in the caller's business; if omitted the contact's latest open ticket is used) — the reply updates the ticket's SLA timers and the response then includes `data` with the ticket's SLA state. `temp_message_id` — your optimistic-bubble id, echoed on the stored message and the realtime event. `body` may contain tracked-link placeholders, which are rewritten to per-contact tracking URLs.

### Errors — read `success`, not the HTTP status
Refusals **before** the send have their own status codes (400 validation, 403, 404, 422 media). Everything decided by the send pipeline — closed 24-hour window, wallet balance, unpaid-bill suspension, DND, Direct Send rejection, provider/Meta errors — comes back as **HTTP 200 with `success: false`** and a human-readable `message` (`error` holds Meta's error object when the provider returned one).

Note: the DND list only blocks *marketing* sends, so it never blocks this endpoint's session messages; a contact blocked via *Block contact* is blocked on WhatsApp's side and surfaces as a provider error.

`ticket_id`, when given, must be a ticket you can reach **and** belong to this contact; otherwise validation fails (**400**, `errors.ticket_id`).

### Safe retries
Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (any unique string per message, e.g. a UUID) — or just a `temp_message_id`, which is used as the key when the header is absent. Keys are per signed-in account and kept for 24 hours.
* **Repeat of a key that was sent:** nothing is sent again; the first response is returned unchanged with header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Retry freely after a timeout.
* **Repeat while the first is still going out:** **409** `{success:false, status:false, code:"send_in_progress"}` — wait and retry.
* **A send that failed** (any non-success answer) releases its key, so retrying with the same key sends.
* **No key:** every request sends, as before.

### Confirmation
A successful send returns `sent_message`: the saved message in exactly the row shape of *Get messages*, plus `temp_message_id` echoed back. Replace your optimistic bubble with it; no need to wait for the realtime event or reload history. It is `null` only if the provider accepted the message but nothing was stored.

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `waba_user_id` | integer | yes | must be a number the caller owns/acts under (else 403) | Sending number id — use `{{waba_user_id}}`. |
| `wa_id` | string | yes | required\|string; must match contact_id | Recipient WhatsApp id (country code + number, no +). |
| `contact_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|owned contact | Contact id. |
| `message_type` | string | yes | required\|string | text \| address \| location \| send_location \| single_product \| multiple_product \| catalogue \| call_permission_request (anything else = text). Overridden when `media` is attached. |
| `body` | string | no | nullable\|string | Text / caption / interactive body. Trimmed. |
| `media` | file | no | nullable\|file; image jpeg/jpg/png ≤5MB, video 3gp/mp4 ≤16MB, document pdf/doc/docx/xls/xlsx/ppt/pptx/txt ≤100MB | multipart only. Type is detected from MIME. |
| `contextual_reply_id` | string | no | none | wamid of the message being replied to (text messages only). |
| `address_country` | string | no | required_if:message_type,address | ISO-2 country for address request. |
| `header` | string | no | none | Header text (address, multiple_product). |
| `footer` | string | no | none | Footer text (address, single_product, multiple_product, catalogue). |
| `singleProduct` | integer | no | required_if:message_type,single_product,catalogue\|nullable\|integer | Product id (single_product) or thumbnail product id (catalogue). |
| `multipleProduct` | string | no | required_if:message_type,multiple_product | Comma-separated product ids. |
| `catalog_id` | string | no | none | Meta catalogue id for single_product / multiple_product. |
| `location` | object|string | no | required_if:message_type,send_location | {latitude, longitude, name, address}; a JSON string is accepted (multipart). |
| `ticket_id` | integer | no | nullable\|integer\|owned ticket | Ticket the reply belongs to. |
| `temp_message_id` | string | no | none | Your optimistic bubble's id. Echoed on the realtime events and in `sent_message`, and used as the retry key when no `Idempotency-Key` header is sent. |
| `direct_send_category` | string | no | nullable\|in:utility,authentication | Direct Send category (text only). |
| `direct_send_ttl` | integer | no | nullable\|integer; utility 30–43200, authentication 30–900 | Time to live, seconds. |
| `direct_send_template_name` | string | no | nullable\|string; utility only; ^[a-z0-9_]+$; ≤512 | Name for the template Meta generates. |

request.description:
Sends an approved template to a contact — the only way to (re)open a conversation outside the 24-hour window. The template is built from its stored components (`rowdata`, see *Get a template*) plus the values in `variables`.

**Required:** `waba_user_id` (the number in `X-Waba-User-Id`; anything else → **403** empty message), `template_id` (a template on that number; otherwise **404** empty message) and `phone_number` (recipient wa_id). `contact_id` is optional — when omitted the contact is looked up by `phone_number`; it is used for the bot-handover check, ticket linking and tracked-link attribution.

### `variables` (object)
| key | used for |
|---|---|
| `mediaTemplate.header_media.file_url` | IMAGE / VIDEO / DOCUMENT header link (upload first with *Upload a media file*) |
| `mediaTemplate.header_media.new_file_name` (or `file_name`) | DOCUMENT header filename |
| `header_text` | TEXT header variable |
| `headerLocation` `{latitude, longitude, name, address}` | LOCATION header |
| `bodyText` | array of body variable values, in order (`{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, …) |
| `tracked_body_links` | `{ "<variable number>": <tracked link id> }` — fills that body variable with a per-contact tracking URL instead of a typed value |
| `otp` | AUTHENTICATION templates: the code (body + copy-code URL button) |
| `limited_time_offer` | LTO templates: expiry date-time string |
| `button_url_text` | dynamic URL button suffix; for limited-time-offer templates, the coupon code |
| `tracked_link_id` | re-point a tracked URL button to another of this number's tracked links |
| `mediaTemplate.carousel` | `{ "1": {file_url}, "2": {file_url}, … }` card header media (1-based) |
| `carousel_body_text` | array per card (0-based) of body values |
| `card_button` | carousel card URL button value |

Catalog buttons and Flow buttons are filled automatically.

### `error_variable` (array, optional)
Tells the server which parts are mandatory for this template, so it validates them before sending: `header_media`, `header_text`, `header_location`, `body_text`, `limited_time_offer`, `button_url_text`, `card_header_media`, `card_body_text`, `card_button_text`. A missing one returns **422** `{status:false, message}` with the first error.

Other optional fields: `ticket_id` (else the contact's latest open ticket; response then includes `ticket_data` with SLA state), `temp_message_id`.

### Errors
403 bot-handled conversation / ticket permission. Any refusal from the send pipeline or provider — insufficient wallet, unpaid-bill suspension, DND (marketing templates to a DND contact), number not onboarded, Meta errors — returns **400** `{status:false, message, error}`. Templates are exempt from the 24-hour-window check. Responses here carry `status` (no `success` key).

`ticket_id`, when given, must be a ticket you can reach and belong to this contact (**404** otherwise).

### Safe retries
Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (any unique string per message, e.g. a UUID) — or just a `temp_message_id`, which is used as the key when the header is absent. Keys are per signed-in account and kept for 24 hours.
* **Repeat of a key that was sent:** nothing is sent again; the first response is returned unchanged with header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Retry freely after a timeout.
* **Repeat while the first is still going out:** **409** `{success:false, status:false, code:"send_in_progress"}` — wait and retry.
* **A send that failed** (any non-success answer) releases its key, so retrying with the same key sends.
* **No key:** every request sends, as before.

### Confirmation
A successful send returns `sent_message`: the saved message in exactly the row shape of *Get messages*, plus `temp_message_id` echoed back. Replace your optimistic bubble with it; no need to wait for the realtime event or reload history. It is `null` only if the provider accepted the message but nothing was stored.

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `waba_user_id` | integer | yes | must be a number the caller owns/acts under (else 403) | Sending number — `{{waba_user_id}}`. |
| `template_id` | integer | yes | template on this number (else 404) | Template id. |
| `phone_number` | string | yes | not validated | Recipient wa_id (country code + number, no +). |
| `contact_id` | integer | no | not validated; scoped lookup | Contact id; resolved from phone_number when omitted. |
| `variables` | object | no | see table | Values for header/body/buttons/carousel. |
| `error_variable` | array<string> | no | values listed above | Which variables to enforce as required. |
| `ticket_id` | integer | no | ticket in caller's business | Ticket to attribute the reply to. |
| `temp_message_id` | string | no | none | Your optimistic bubble's id. Echoed on the realtime events and in `sent_message`, and used as the retry key when no `Idempotency-Key` header is sent. |

variable.description: Ticket id (tkt_ticket.id). Must belong to the caller's business, otherwise 404.

request.description:
**Permission:** any one of `list-ticket-inbox`, `create-ticket-inbox`, `edit-ticket-inbox`, `delete-ticket-inbox` (route middleware).

Reassigns the ticket. Also assigns the contact (adds the user in multi-assignment mode, otherwise sets the contact's single assignee), writes a change-log line ('This ticket is assigned to X (previously assigned to Y)'), fires `contact_updated` (and `agent_abandoned` when it moved away from a previous agent) automations, and broadcasts the change log and ticket list update.

**Who may assign to whom:** `user_id` must be you or someone in your assign list (**Users** — `GET inbox/users`), and if the ticket is already assigned you must be allowed to manage its current assignee. Anyone who can see an unassigned ticket can claim it. Otherwise **403**. `user_id` must be a user of the caller's business.

**Which tickets you can reach.** Every endpoint that takes a ticket id uses one rule, the same one the list uses: the ticket must be on your business and the selected number; a manager or sub-user also sees only their own tickets, their team's tickets in their Allowed Ticketing Departments, unassigned tickets in those departments, and unassigned tickets in the number's default department. A ticket with no department counts as in every department. Business owner, number account and super-admin see every ticket of the number. A ticket outside that rule is a **404**.

**Permission:** `list-ticket-inbox|create-ticket-inbox|edit-ticket-inbox|delete-ticket-inbox`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `user_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|exists:users,id where business_user_id = caller's business | New assignee. |

request.description:
**Permission:** any one of `list-ticket-inbox`, `create-ticket-inbox`, `edit-ticket-inbox`, `delete-ticket-inbox` (route middleware).

Changes the ticket status. Caller must be able to manage the ticket (the assignee, an ancestor of the assignee, or the business; unassigned tickets only by business/admin/reseller) — else 403. Same status → `{success:true}` with no change. Moving to a closed status sets `closed_at` and records the resolution metric; moving to an open status clears `closed_at`. Reopening (closed → open) is refused with 422 if the contact already has another open ticket. Writes a change-log line and broadcasts. Validation errors return **400** with `errors` only (no `message`).

**Which tickets you can reach.** Every endpoint that takes a ticket id uses one rule, the same one the list uses: the ticket must be on your business and the selected number; a manager or sub-user also sees only their own tickets, their team's tickets in their Allowed Ticketing Departments, unassigned tickets in those departments, and unassigned tickets in the number's default department. A ticket with no department counts as in every department. Business owner, number account and super-admin see every ticket of the number. A ticket outside that rule is a **404**.

**Permission:** `list-ticket-inbox|create-ticket-inbox|edit-ticket-inbox|delete-ticket-inbox`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|exists:tkt_statuses,id where waba_user_id = active number | New status (see Get ticket metadata). |

request.description:
**Permission:** any one of `list-ticket-inbox`, `create-ticket-inbox`, `edit-ticket-inbox`, `delete-ticket-inbox` (route middleware).

Copies selected messages of a **closed** ticket into a brand-new ticket for the same contact (all timestamps = now, copies get `message_id = null`). Status/priority come from the request, then channel-config defaults, then the original; department and assignee default to the original's. SLA is recalculated asynchronously for the new ticket (so SLA columns are absent/null in the response). Change logs are written on both tickets; the new ticket is broadcast to other agents.

Checks, in order: validation (**422**, `errors` only), ticket ownership (404), manage-ticket permission (403), ticket must be closed (422), contact has no other open ticket (422), at least one `message_ids` belongs to this ticket (422; ids from other tickets are silently dropped). The 500 message includes the exception text. Returns only the serialized new ticket's set columns plus `assign_user`, `status`, `contact`.

**Which tickets you can reach.** Every endpoint that takes a ticket id uses one rule, the same one the list uses: the ticket must be on your business and the selected number; a manager or sub-user also sees only their own tickets, their team's tickets in their Allowed Ticketing Departments, unassigned tickets in those departments, and unassigned tickets in the number's default department. A ticket with no department counts as in every department. Business owner, number account and super-admin see every ticket of the number. A ticket outside that rule is a **404**.

`assign_user_id`, when given, must be you or someone in your assign list (**403** otherwise); a manager or sub-user may only pick a `department_id` from their Allowed Ticketing Departments or the default department.

**Permission:** `list-ticket-inbox|create-ticket-inbox|edit-ticket-inbox|delete-ticket-inbox`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `message_ids` | array<integer> | yes | required\|array\|min:1; each integer | Message row ids (messages.id, as returned by Get ticket messages) to copy. |
| `subject` | string | yes | required\|string\|max:255 | Subject of the new ticket. |
| `department_id` | integer | no | nullable\|integer\|exists:departments,id (same WhatsApp number) | Default: original ticket's department. |
| `status_id` | integer | no | nullable\|integer\|exists:tkt_statuses,id (same WhatsApp number) | Default: config default, then original. |
| `priority_id` | integer | no | nullable\|integer\|exists:tkt_priorities,id | Default: config default, then original. |
| `assign_user_id` | integer | no | nullable\|integer\|exists:users,id where business_user_id = caller's business | Default: original assignee. |

Media is collected from the ticket's messages on the active WhatsApp number: image/video/document messages (local file, or downloaded from Meta by media id and cached), template and interactive headers with image/video, and text messages that are a bare URL (type `link`). Items whose file is not on disk are skipped. `media_size` is human-readable (`UNKNOWN` for template headers; absent for links). The ticket id is not ownership-checked; an id not on this number simply returns no items.

**Which tickets you can reach.** Every endpoint that takes a ticket id uses one rule, the same one the list uses: the ticket must be on your business and the selected number; a manager or sub-user also sees only their own tickets, their team's tickets in their Allowed Ticketing Departments, unassigned tickets in those departments, and unassigned tickets in the number's default department. Media panel tabs: `media` (images + videos), `document`, or `link`, optionally filtered by a case-insensitive substring of the file name/URL, newest first. Validation failure returns **400** with the first error as `message` (no `errors` object).

Media is collected from the ticket's messages on the active WhatsApp number: image/video/document messages (local file, or downloaded from Meta by media id and cached), template and interactive headers with image/video, and text messages that are a bare URL (type `link`). Items whose file is not on disk are skipped. `media_size` is human-readable (`UNKNOWN` for template headers; absent for links). The ticket id is not ownership-checked; an id not on this number simply returns no items.

A ticket with no department counts as in every department. Business owner, number account and super-admin see every ticket of the number. A ticket outside that rule is a **404**.

request.description:
**Permission:** any one of `list-ticket-inbox`, `create-ticket-inbox`, `edit-ticket-inbox`, `delete-ticket-inbox` (route middleware).

Paged ticket list for the ticket inbox sidebar, scoped to the caller's business and active WhatsApp number. Managers and sub-users only see tickets assigned inside their own hierarchy (except on the `unassigned` tab), and only within their Allowed Ticketing Departments (see below). Unassigned tickets in a closed status are never returned. Sorted by `last_replied_at` descending.

`total_unread` is the **total row count for the current tab/filters** (used for infinite scroll), not an unread count. `unread_message_count` is capped at 99. `display_wa_id` is the masked number (number masking settings).

No validation: all fields are optional and invalid values simply match nothing. `tags` must be a JSON array to apply. The serialized eager loads use snake_case keys (`assign_user`, `last_thread`); the controller also adds `assignTo` (same object). User object is the full `users` row minus hidden fields (password, tokens); only common keys shown. Contact is the full per-business contact row (contacts_masters_{business}); only common columns shown.

A ticket with no department counts as in every department. Business owner, number account and super-admin see every ticket of the number. A ticket outside that rule is a **404**.

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ticket_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer | Ticket id owned by the caller's business. |

request.description:
**Permission:** any one of `list-ticket-inbox`, `create-ticket-inbox`, `edit-ticket-inbox`, `delete-ticket-inbox` (route middleware).

Manually opens a WhatsApp ticket for a contact. Missing department/status/priority fall back to the WhatsApp channel configuration defaults. Ticket number comes from the channel's sequence (e.g. `TKT-000124`); with no channel config it falls back to `TKT` + 4 random digits and no SLA. With a config, SLA is calculated synchronously. Creates the metrics row, a 'Ticket created by …' change log, syncs tags and adds an optional first note, then broadcasts the new ticket.

Rejected with 422 if the contact already has an open ticket (no status, or a status not flagged closed) on this number. Validation failures also return **422** with `{success, message, errors}`.

**Rules:** the contact must belong to the selected number (otherwise **404 Contact not found**); `assign_user_id` must be you or someone in your assign list (otherwise **403**); a manager or sub-user may only pick a `department_id` from their Allowed Ticketing Departments or the number's default department (otherwise **422**). `ticket_create_metadata` only offers those departments.

**Permission:** `list-ticket-inbox|create-ticket-inbox|edit-ticket-inbox|delete-ticket-inbox`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contact_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer; must exist in the caller's business contacts (else 404) | Contact id. |
| `subject` | string | yes | required\|string\|max:255 | Ticket subject. |
| `department_id` | integer | no | nullable\|integer\|exists:departments,id (same WhatsApp number) | Default: channel config default_department_id. |
| `status_id` | integer | no | nullable\|integer\|exists:tkt_statuses,id (same WhatsApp number) | Default: channel config default_status_id. |
| `priority_id` | integer | no | nullable\|integer\|exists:tkt_priorities,id | Default: channel config default_priority_id. |
| `assign_user_id` | integer | yes | required\|integer\|exists:users,id where business_user_id = caller's business | Assignee. |
| `tags` | array<integer> | no | nullable\|array; each integer\|exists:tags,id (same WhatsApp number) | Tags to attach. |
| `notes` | string | no | nullable\|string | Optional first internal note. |

request.description:
**Permission:** any one of `list-ticket-inbox`, `create-ticket-inbox`, `edit-ticket-inbox`, `delete-ticket-inbox` (route middleware).

Creates a contact on the active WhatsApp number from the 'New ticket' form. A leading `+` is stripped from `phone`; the country code (default `91`) is prefixed unless the number already starts with it, and the result is stored as `wa_id` and `phone`. Returns 422 if that number already exists on this WhatsApp number. Validation failures return **422**; the 500 message includes the exception text.

**Permission:** `list-ticket-inbox|create-ticket-inbox|edit-ticket-inbox|delete-ticket-inbox`

**Request fields**

| Field | Type | Required | Rules | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | required\|string\|max:255 | Stored as profile_name. |
| `phone` | string | yes | required\|string\|min:8 | Phone number, with or without country code / leading +. |
| `country` | string | no | nullable\|string\|max:10, default '91' | Dialling code without + (e.g. 91). |
